Understanding the motherboard.
Let's go over the basic components of a motherboard by looking at an example.
I work at a hardware service shop.
We build and repair many computers.
A customer wants me to build a computer with this motherboard.
Let's take a look at it.
It is an H310B4 desktop motherboard that my customer bought online.
Do you see the large square with the silver-colored edges?
There, a little above the middle of the motherboard.
That's the CPU socket where the CPU, the central processing unit, goes.
Always make sure that you have a CPU that is compatible with the motherboard.
This motherboard is compatible with Intel Core i3, i5, and i7 processors and Celeron and Pentax.
Processors.
After we install a CPU, we need to also install some kind of heatsink over the CPU because it gets really hot.
We'll do that later.
Now, look to the right of the CPU socket.
There are two long black slots.
These are slots for the DIM memory.
DIM stands for Dual Inline Memory Module.
These modules hold the RAM or random access memory and provide short-term memory for the computer.
This motherboard is designed for double data rate 4 or DDR4 RAM.
It is very fast.
We'll install two 16 gigabyte DIM units for a total of 32 gigabytes of memory.
Next, look at the bottom of the motherboard.
Do you see the long slot at the very bottom?
It says M2 over the slot.
This is the PCIe slot.
Here you can install various hardware like graphics processing units or GPUs for short.
This motherboard is designed for installing an M2 solid-state drive or SSD here.
M2 SSDs can transfer 32 gigabytes of data per second.
This one uses SATA 3 controllers, so it is very fast.
Don't worry too much about all these details.

three SATA sockets.

There are some ports where you can connect your peripherals.
On this motherboard, the lower connector with the red, green, and blue ports is for audio.
You can connect speakers or headphones here.
